item.title: What the CMMC Pause Means for the Defense Industrial Base
item.description: The Pentagon has paused its contractor cybersecurity certification program amid concerns from small businesses. What does the decision mean, and how can the department strengthen supply chain cybersecurity without imposing unsustainable burdens on smaller contractors?

item.title: Tariff Follies Scene 47
item.description: In this week's column, Bill Reinsch provides an assessment of the Trump administration's trade policy: its objectives, implementation, and evolution.

item.title: Taiwan Needs an AI Cyber Shield Now to Defend Against Invasion
item.description: China attempts over 2.6 million cyber intrusions daily into Taiwan’s networks. Taiwan should adopt the United Kingdom’s newest AI cyber shield concept, developing its own nationally integrated AI cybersecurity system to disrupt China’s reunification efforts.

item.title: States Weekly: July 29, 2026
item.description: This edition of States Weekly covers July 29, 2026.

item.title: Red Kraken: The Coming Age of Agentic Cyber Strategy
item.description: In a tabletop exercise, members of Congress faced Red Kraken, an AI agent trained to emulate Beijing. Benjamin Jensen and Emily Harding examine how China could target ports and logistics to delay U.S. mobilization and argue for AI-enabled gaming to strengthen cyber defenses.

item.title: Is U.S. Haiti Policy an Opportunity for Success?
item.description: Amid the costly on-and-off conflict with Iran, U.S. foreign policymakers would do well to refocus attention on the Caribbean. Haiti might offer the best opportunity for positive change.

item.title: Japan’s Defense Industry Charts an Uncertain Global Path
item.description: With the Mogami frigate sale to Australia and the end of decades-old restrictions, Tokyo's manufacturers are entering the world market as both partner and rival to allied producers —a tension Washington and its friends must now learn to manage.

item.title: Come Hague or High Seas: China’s Environmental Legacy in the South China Sea
item.description: As China positions itself as a leader of global ocean governance, the findings from the 2016 South China Sea tribunal ruling take on a renewed significance.
